proposal.utterance: Classify 'a legal duty' in BFO top-level terms. Is it a continuant or an occurrent, and what subtype?

entities.label: LegalDuty
entities.rationale: A legal duty is a specifically dependent continuant: it cannot exist without a bearer (some agent on whom the duty falls), it persists through time (continuant), and it is externally grounded — its normative force derives from legal recognition/social institutional facts rather than from internal physical constitution of the bearer. This matches BFO Role (BFO_0000023). It is closely analogous to the existing working:LegalObligation, which is already typed as BFO_0000023. The user asks for a classification of 'a legal duty' as a kind, so this is a new class. Note: working:LegalObligation already covers much of this territory; see open_questions.

relations.rationale: Legal duty is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023): a specifically dependent continuant that is externally grounded in institutional/legal facts and inheres in an agent-bearer.
Role is itself a subclass of Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020), so LegalDuty inherits this classification, confirming it is a continuant, not an occurrent.

open_questions: working:LegalObligation already exists as a BFO_0000023 (Role) class. Should working:LegalDuty be treated as a synonym/equivalent class of working:LegalObligation, or is there a intended distinction (e.g., duty as a more specific or narrower concept than obligation)?
Should LegalDuty be modeled as a subclass of working:LegalObligation rather than directly under BFO_0000023, if the intent is that all duties are obligations but not all obligations are duties?

Is the bearer of a legal duty always a legal person/agent (individual or corporate), or can it include non-persons? This affects whether a domain restriction on RO_0000052 (inheres in) is appropriate.
proposal.rationale_summary: A legal duty is a CONTINUANT (BFO_0000002), specifically a Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020), and more precisely a Role (BFO_0000023). The argument is as follows: (1) It is not an occurrent — it does not unfold or happen in time as a process; it persists as long as the normative relationship holds. (2) It is not an independent continuant — it cannot exist without an agent who bears it. (3) Among specifically dependent continuants, it is not a Quality (BFO_0000019) because it does not measure an intrinsic property, nor a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because its grounds are not internal to the bearer. (4) It is a Role (BFO_0000023) because its normative force is entirely externally grounded in the legal-institutional system — the bearer acquires the duty through legal recognition, not through any intrinsic property. This mirrors the existing working:LegalObligation class. A potential new class working:LegalDuty is proposed but may be redundant with working:LegalObligation; the user should confirm whether to reuse, equate, or differentiate.
